> [!NOTE] > ## Reviews paused > > It looks like this branch is under active development. To avoid overwhelming you with review comments due to an influx of new commits, CodeRabbit has automatically paused this review. You can configure this behavior by changing the `reviews.auto_review.auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits` setting. > > Use the following commands to manage reviews: > - `@coderabbitai resume` to resume automatic reviews. > - `@coderabbitai review` to trigger a single review. > > Use the checkboxes below for quick actions: > - [ ] ▶️ Resume reviews > - [ ] 🔍 Trigger review ## Walkthrough Teardown and cleanup in Gateway API tests were changed: upgrade teardown no longer polls for Gateway removal and now waits for gateway-associated Deployment deletion. The suite no longer enforces ordered/serial execution; shared bulk Gateway deletion was removed in favor of per-test deferred `deleteGateway` and new helpers. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Upgrade test teardown**
`test/extended/router/gatewayapi_upgrade.go`|Removed the Gateway polling loop and the `wait` import in teardown. Teardown now calls `waitForGatewayDeploymentDeletion(t.oc, t.gatewayName)` and fails the test on deployment-cleanup errors instead of best-effort polling.| |**Controller tests & helpers**
`test/extended/router/gatewayapicontroller.go`|Removed `g.Ordered`/`g.Serial` from `g.Describe`; eliminated shared `AfterEach` bulk Gateway deletion and moved to per-test `defer deleteGateway(oc, gw)`. Added `waitForGatewayDeploymentDeletion(oc *exutil.CLI, gatewayName string) error` to poll for the Gateway-associated Deployment deletion, and `deleteGateway(oc *exutil.CLI, gatewayName string)` to delete Gateway and wait for deployment removal (failing the test on errors).| ## Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Test as Test participant API as API Server participant Controller as Gateway Controller participant Kube as Kubernetes (Deployments) Test->>API: delete Gateway API-->>Test: acknowledge deletion Controller->>Kube: reconcile -> delete Deployment for Gateway Kube-->>Controller: Deployment deleted Test->>Controller: call waitForGatewayDeploymentDeletion(gatewayName) Controller->>API: Get Deployment status API-->>Controller: NotFound => return success Controller-->>Test: success / error ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~22 minutes
🚥 Pre-merge checks | ✅ 9 | ❌ 1 ### ❌ Failed checks (1 warning) | Check name | Status | Explanation | Resolution | | :----------------: | :--------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Docstring Coverage | ⚠️ Warning | Docstring coverage is 50.00% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. | Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold. |
✅ Passed checks (9 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :----------------------------------------------: | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Stable And Deterministic Test Names | ✅ Passed | All test names in modified files are static, deterministic strings with no dynamic information such as timestamps, UUIDs, pod names, or generated identifiers. | | Test Structure And Quality | ✅ Passed | Test changes implement proper cleanup mechanisms with defer statements, new helper functions with timeout handling, and descriptive error messages following Ginkgo best practices. | | Microshift Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | Both the upgrade and controller Gateway API tests include the [apigroup:gateway.networking.k8s.io] tag, causing MicroShift CI to automatically skip them. | | Single Node Openshift (Sno) Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The pull request modifies gateway API test cleanup behavior without introducing multi-node or HA cluster assumptions. Changes are purely about improving test cleanup mechanics and do not affect SNO compatibility. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The PR modifies only test suite files in test/extended/router/ without introducing any deployment manifests, operator code, or scheduling constraints. | | Ote Binary Stdout Contract | ✅ Passed | The modified files are Ginkgo test utility files that do not write to stdout. No main(), TestMain(), or process-level initialization functions found. Helper functions use e2e.Logf and e2e.Failf which are Ginkgo-intercepted logging utilities that do not write to stdout. No fmt.Print*, log.Print*, klog, or os.Stdout calls detected. | | Ipv6 And Disconnected Network Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | PR does not add new Ginkgo e2e test cases, only modifies existing tests and adds utility helper functions without IPv4 assumptions. | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The title accurately describes the main change: fixing gateway cleanup in parallel e2e test workers by implementing explicit per-test cleanup and centralized deletion logic. | | Description Check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped - CodeRabbit’s high-level summary is enabled. |

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/31023):

>The Gateway API controller tests tracked Gateways in a sharedin-memory gateways slice, deleting them during AfterEach cleanup. However, openshift-tests distributes tests across separate parallel worker processes. The annotation-based checkAllTestsDone coordination works correctly because annotations are stored on the cluster-scoped GatewayClass, but the gateways slice is not shared across processes. The process that runs the final AfterEach cleanup has an empty gateways slice, so it deletes the GatewayClass and istiod but never deletes the Gateways created by other processes. This leaves gateway deployments orphaned on the cluster.
>
>As a secondary issue, even when gateways were deleted, the GatewayClass and istiod were removed without waiting for the gateway proxy deployments to be fully cleaned up by GC. Since the deployments have an owner reference to the Gateway (not a finalizer), the cascade deletion is asynchronous, creating a race where gateway pods lose their control plane and crash-loop.
>
>Fix both issues by cleaning up gateways at the individual test level using defer deleteGateway, which deletes the Gateway and waits for its proxy deployment to be removed by GC. Add deleteGateway and waitForGatewayDeploymentDeletion helpers shared by both the controller tests and the upgrade test Teardown. Cleanup errors now hard fail to surface leftover resources immediately rather than causing confusing downstream test failures.
>
